premium_plus: private virtual office, multiple individually admitted guests

existing_accounts: Migration 1522 freezes the existing user population and grants Premium Plus once. New accounts default to Basic. Existing AuricWell accounts retain this grant when their shared provider identity is connected.
identity: Personal supervision and team email tokens exchange for scoped, roster-checked identity without creating an app login. The email says not to share or forward the link.
Unsigned visitors using shared calendar URLs are guests with independent opaque credentials; they receive no staff attendance credit or client identity from their display name.
Signed-in calendar visitors use their account and existing roster checks. Cached personal grants are not attached on shared calendar routes.
Supervision calendar attachments and calendar composer links use shared meeting references, never personal invitation tokens.
Interview calendars use a separate signed calendar reference instead of the candidate bearer token. Candidate email links remain personal.
Client invitation-to-client binding is preserved; regression tests pass.
Calendar guests follow the ordinary meeting waiting-room policy. Supervision transcription pauses while an admitted anonymous calendar guest cannot be tied to a signed supervision agreement.
office: Stable provider URL exposed by a top Meetings button with hover details.
Guest camera snapshot and acknowledgement required; images encrypted at rest and disclosed only to the owning provider.
Unpredictable guest credentials protect status and video requests. Public form fields cannot assign client or staff IDs.
Provider must connect first. Office has no open-room or admit-all endpoint.
Admission and token issue use an office row transaction lock. Premium admits one guest; Premium Plus allows additional individually admitted guests.
Ending or reopening a stale office rotates the media session and invalidates prior visit admissions; completed visit snapshots are removed.
No automatic clinical recording in a private office; a photo and display name do not bind a guest to a client chart.
